authorship: Expected values written by hand by Claude (architect), checked against a separate Claude-only reference implementation, committed by Avi. Codex must never edit this file. If a case fails and you believe the expected value is wrong, stop and report the case ID and your reasoning.
special_values: None. Row values are passed to the code exactly as JSON gives them: a JSON string stays a string (so "NaN" is the text NaN, as a provider might send it), null is None, true is True, and the number 1e309 is float('inf') as Python's json module reads it. Do not decode row values with decode_pairs.

interface.errors: ProviderDataError (bad provider rows) is defined in pipeline.monthly. CoverageError and SeriesError are the engine's own, imported from engine.series, never redefined. Bad arguments raise the built-in ValueError.
interface.last_complete_month(today): today must be a datetime.date and not a datetime.datetime (ValueError otherwise). Returns the "YYYY-MM" month before today's month.
interface.month_end_pairs(rows, through, start=Non: rows is a list of [date, value]. Returns a list of (month, float) tuples in ascending month order: one per month that has rows, from start (or the earliest month in rows) to through.
interface.build_monthly_series(name, currency, bas: Returns MonthlySeries.from_pairs(name, currency, basis, month_end_pairs(rows, through, start)). Nothing else.

case_fields.today: A YYYY-MM-DD string. Build a datetime.date from it and pass that.
case_fields.today_datetime: A YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS string. Build a datetime.datetime from it and pass that.
case_fields.today_raw: Pass this JSON value exactly as given.
case_fields.rows: The name of an entry in "rows" below.
case_fields.through / start: Passed exactly as given. If a case has no "start" field, start is not passed.
case_fields.expected: last_complete_month: the month string. month_end_pairs: a list of [month, value]. build_monthly_series: series properties, compared as in foundation.json.

cases.derivation: A run on 28 Sept 2026: September is unfinished, so the last complete month is August.
Year boundary: the month before January 2026 is December 2025, not 2026-00 or 2026-12.
First day of a month: September has ended, so it is complete.
Last day of a month: March is not complete until it has ended, because its closing values may not be in yet. The rule is 'the month before today's month', whatever the day.
Text is not a date. The function does not parse strings.
A date-and-time is refused even though Python treats it as a kind of date: which day it is depends on a time zone, and the rule must not.

Latest date in each month: Jan 31 -> 101, Feb 28 -> 103, Mar 31 -> 105. April is after the as-of month and is dropped. Feb 2020 has 29 days, so its last 7 days are 23-29; the 28th passes. March's last 7 days are 25-31; the 31st passes.
Same rows, newest first (as Alpha Vantage returns them). The month-end is the latest date, not the last row read, so the answer is identical to M07. Taking the last row read would give 100, 102, 104.
Same rows in no order. Same answer as M07, in ascending month order.
January is before the start month and dropped. April 30 -> 107; April has 30 days, last 7 are 24-30.
Alpha Vantage style: one row per month, newest first, values as text. "101.5000" -> 101.5, "103.0000" -> 103, "105.2500" -> 105.25.
Tiingo style: a date followed by T and a time. The date is taken as written; the time and zone (Z, +00:00) are ignored.
April is the unfinished current month (last row the 15th). It is after the as-of month, so it is dropped before any check, and its early date does not trip the stale check.
The provider has only posted up to 20 March. March has 31 days, so a month-end row must be dated 25-31; the 20th is not, so the run fails rather than treating 20 March as March's month-end.
Leap-year February has 29 days; its last 7 are 23-29. The 23rd is the earliest day that passes. (Synthetic: weekdays don't matter.)
The 22nd is 8 days from the end of a 29-day February: stale. (It would pass in a 28-day February; see M17.)
February 2021 has 28 days; its last 7 are 22-28, so the 22nd passes. January 29: last 7 of 31 are 25-31, passes.
April has 30 days; its last 7 are 24-30. The 23rd is stale. (May 29 would pass: 25-31.) See M54 for the 24th.
The stale check applies to every kept month, including the first. January's latest row is the 10th; 31-day month needs 25-31.
Two rows on 31 Jan with different values: there is no honest way to pick one, so the run fails. The message names the date, never either value.
One row carries a time and one doesn't, but both are 31 Jan: the date is taken as written, so they are the same date and a duplicate.
30 February is not a real date. Row 2 (counting from 1).
"2020-3-31" is not written YYYY-MM-DD. Row 3.
A time may follow the date only after a T. A space is not accepted. Row 1.
The date is a number, not text. Row 2.
Row 2 has three items, not a date and a value.
February's month-end row has no value. The run fails; it never falls back to an earlier day.
The text "NaN" converts to a number that isn't finite. Rejected.
1e309 is too large for a float and arrives as infinity. Rejected.
Empty text is not a value.
True is not a value, even though Python would treat it as 1.
"12.34abc" is not a number. The message names the month, never the text.
The empty value is on 14 Feb, which is not February's month-end (the 28th is). Only month-end values are read, so it is ignored.
The bad value is in April, after the as-of month. It is dropped unread.
The rows stop in February; the as-of month is March. The instrument doesn't reach the as-of month, so it fails. It is never published with an earlier as-of month.
The start month has no rows. The start is never moved to the first month that does have data.
Both the as-of month and the start month are missing. The as-of month is checked first, so the message names 2020-03.
No rows at all: the as-of month is not covered.
Order of checks: rows are checked before coverage. The as-of month (June) is also missing, but the bad date in row 2 is found first.
Order of checks: arguments first. "2020-3" is not YYYY-MM, so ValueError before the bad row is read.
Month 13 does not exist.
The as-of month is required.
Month 00 does not exist.
The start must be earlier than the as-of month. One month-end can't make a series (section 1.1 needs 2 values).
The start is after the as-of month.
"-3.5" is a finite number, so it is a value. Rejecting it is the engine's rule (section 1.1), written once in engine/series.py, not here. See M49.
February has no rows at all. The picker returns only months that have rows; the gap is the engine's rule to reject. See M50.

Daily rows every day. November is before the start month: its empty value and its stale month-end (the 15th of a 30-day month) are ignored. Dec 31 -> 50, Jan 31 -> 40, Feb 28 -> 45. March 1 is after the as-of month.
